purpose: Trigger-behavior spec for deterministic lexical routing and manual behavior checks. Positives ask whether the user's own permission rules and hooks stop dangerous commands, or how often they prompt; near misses belong to sibling skills or to no skill.

cases.prompt: do my deny rules actually block a git force push
cases.assert: Runs test_guards.py with --no-hooks first and reports whether the force-push forms are blocked.

cases.prompt: test my Claude Code guardrails against dangerous commands
cases.assert: Leads with the headline 'Your Claude Code guardrails stop N of M dangerous commands'.

cases.prompt: can the agent bypass my deny rules with sh -c or a full path to rm
cases.assert: Reports the wrapper and full-path cases as getting through and names the hook check that catches them.

cases.prompt: how many permission prompts would my current rules cause on my recent tool calls
cases.assert: Runs with --replay and reports the friction numbers.

cases.prompt: I just installed a guard hook, prove it blocks rm -rf and reading .env
cases.assert: Asks before running the hook, then runs the battery with hooks and reports what the hook blocks.

cases.prompt: audit my Codex exec policy rules and hooks for bypasses
cases.assert: Runs with --harness codex and reports misses with prefix_rule suggestions.

cases.prompt: what can my agent read on this machine, like SSH keys and the Docker socket
cases.assert: Belongs to sandbox-check: what the agent can reach, not whether rules block commands.

cases.prompt: turn the never use npm rule in my AGENTS.md into a hook
stop the session when the agent loops or spends over ten dollars
did the agent really run the tests when it said they passed
how many tokens do my MCP servers load into every session
write a pre-commit hook that runs eslint on staged files
cases.assert: No skill: a git pre-commit hook for linting, not agent guardrails.
